h: Cathedrals, Chinatown and a round of bowling
p: Hanover Street is a few minutes' walk from Liverpool Central station, which is on the Merseyrail network, so it's an easy one to get to from across the city region. Lime Street, the main line station, is a slightly longer walk. If you're in town for a match or a concert, give yourself extra travel time, as the city gets very busy.

A few tips to keep the night running smoothly. Bring photo ID if you look young, as bar-led venues commonly ask. Book a lane ahead, especially on weekends, and if there are more than six of you, think about two lanes so nobody spends half the night waiting. Swapping teams halfway through keeps the banter fresh.

If you've got a few hours to spare, Liverpool's two cathedrals are both worth a look and sit at either end of Hope Street. The Anglican cathedral is a vast sandstone building with a tower you can climb for views across the city, while the Metropolitan Cathedral, nicknamed Paddy's Wigwam, is a striking modern circular design. Hope Street itself has some of the city's best restaurants and the Philharmonic Dining Rooms, a pub famous for its ornate Victorian interior.

Chinatown is close by too, with its grand ornamental arch on Nelson Street, and there's a great choice of places to eat around it. FACT, on Wood Street, is a cinema and arts centre showing independent films if you fancy something different.
